title: Home values slump as RBA mulls rate increase
full_text:
The nationwide slump in house values has spread to Brisbane and Perth with no signs the property downturn is close to ending, amid fears it could get worse if the Reserve Bank pushes ahead with another interest rate hike this week.
Figures released today by Cotality show the nation's property values fell another 1.2 per cent in October, the seventh consecutive monthly drop, to be down 6.7 per cent since March. In dollar terms, median property values have slumped by $63,400 or more than $9000 a month.
Sydney's median house price fell another 1.9 per cent through the month to be down by 11.1 per cent since the start of the year. The median unit price dropped by 0.7 per cent to be down by 6.5 per cent.
Melbourne's median house price edged down by 1 per cent to $906,000. It has fallen by 9 per cent this year. The city's median unit price slipped by 0.3 per cent in October and is down by 4.7 per cent since the start of 2026.
But bigger falls are now being recorded across the country in cities which have had the largest increase in values over recent years.
Brisbane's median house value fell by 2 per cent last month and is now the weakest market in the country with values down by 6.2 per cent over the past three months. Perth's median house value fell by 1.7 per cent in October, it slipped by 1.2 per cent in Adelaide while it eased 1 per cent in Canberra.
In April, the median house price was above $1 million in five capitals. Sydney's median, though the highest in the country at $1.6 million, had already been falling for two months, while the other capitals in the $1 million club were Brisbane, Perth, Canberra and Adelaide.
Now just Sydney, at $1.44 million, and Brisbane ($1.1 million) are over the $1 million mark.
Cotality research manager Tim Lawless said it was clear the downturn in the property market had stretched across the country.
"Virtually every suburb across Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide has recorded a drop in values over the past three months," he said.
Two markets defied last month's fall. House values lifted by 0.6 per cent in both Hobart, where the median price is almost $797,000, and in Darwin, where it sits at $745,726.
Across every part of Sydney and Melbourne, values are falling.
In Melbourne, the smallest annual decline has been in the city centre, down by just 0.3 per cent, while values have eased by 0.7 per cent in the outer north-west around Sunbury.
Outside the capitals, most regional areas are still well up on where they were a year ago. They include WA's Goldfields region (up 23.8 per cent), the Darling Downs of Queensland (18.2 per cent), Dubbo in NSW (11.7 per cent) and Victoria's Glenelg region (7.9 per cent).
The pressure on the market is likely to intensify after tomorrow, with financial markets and economists expecting the Reserve Bank's monetary policy board to deliver its fifth rate hike this year.
AMP chief economist Shane Oliver, who expects the bank to take the cash rate to an 18-year high of 4.85 per cent, said a quarter percentage point hike would add about $110 to monthly repayments on an average mortgage, taking the increase this year to $550 a month.
